provisional_claims.summary: Campaign fixes: (1) runtime.execution_version ignored the campaign's recorded release and always executed conservation-2, so classic-1 campaigns used the wrong rain-barrel ecology; (2) publish() accepted stale workers (generation = ? OR owner != ?) so a reclaimed/cancelled lease could overwrite progress; (3) publish committed branch state before writing its checkpoint/report in a second transaction (non-atomic progress history); (4) compact() computed protected descendant origins but deleted them anyway, breaking provenance/fork anchors; (5) fork re-applied treatment events at the checkpoint offset although that care is already part of the checkpoint garden.

Fork of branch with event at offset 4 from checkpoint 4 applied the water twice.

provisional_claims.summary: Ensemble fixes: (1) publish validated only the ticket's previously known reads, so a never-computed node prepared before an edit published results computed from superseded inputs into the new revision (now also checks the reads actually used by the computation); (2) report() replaced the archived envelope's result with a live re-summary of current outcomes, so earlier revision reports changed after later edits; (3) cache hits returned the cached trial's origin identity instead of the requested replicate/treatment identity, so equal source saves under different labels collapsed into one replicate; (4) summarize paired controls.values() positionally with treatment rows instead of pairing each replicate with its own control (wrong/misaligned pairs when a replicate is excluded).
provisional_claims.reproduction: create examples/ensemble.json; prepare a treatment ticket, edit plan:water, publish the stale ticket -> previously accepted (now False). Complete rev 1, edit to rev 2, finish: report(e,1) previously showed rev 2 numbers. Two sources with identical saves: second outcome identity reported the first label. Control of replicate A failing: treatment of B was paired with control of A's slot.

provisional_claims.summary: Staged study fixes: (1) later stages continued every treatment from the previous stage's *control* checkpoint, discarding each treatment's earlier care/results (now each job continues its own treatment's checkpoint, parent anchor names the right treatment); (2) stage decision was finalized as soon as any source had a complete control+treatments set, so worker completion order decided promotions and pending trials were ignored; also a stage with no eligible source never recorded its failed decision (now waits until all stage trials are terminal, then records promotion or failure).
provisional_claims.reproduction: StudyStore.create(**examples/study.json); work_once until None. Before: stage-1 'Compost' job state equalled control's stage-0 checkpoint (compost care lost) and stage 0 report was written after first complete replicate, with remaining jobs still ready; with all controls failing the study stayed 'running' forever. After: reports for both stages, stage 1 jobs' parent digest matches own-treatment checkpoints.

provisional_claims.summary: History fixes: (1) replay resolved references to the author's stale local-ID binding instead of the logical object's current ID, so after a correction renumbered objects later actions edited the wrong/unrelated object; (2) replay checkpoint cache key used only the last event (events[-1:]) so different prefixes ending in the same event (e.g. after a correction) reused a stale cached garden; (3) cherry_pick identified events by command digest so independently authored identical actions were merged; now by event identity; (4) rebase order check only considered the target's order, never detecting contradictory local orders of shared events; (5) correct() canonicalized numeric IDs in replacements against the final garden instead of the garden at that point in the history; (6) rebase used the parent's current head as base instead of the fork's recorded base_revision.
provisional_claims.reproduction: create; append note A, note B, edit_note(ident=B's id); correct({A: None}) -> edit_note applied to id 2 (absent / wrong object) -> conflicted; now edits B (id 1) and verify() matches. Cherry-pick two independently authored identical 'water' events from two branches -> second dropped. Fork, append to parent, rebase fork onto another branch -> base taken from parent's moved head, parent's new events treated as local deletions.

provisional_claims.summary: Field courier CRDT fixes: precedes() iterated the wrong clock's peers (events from peers absent in another context counted as superseded); concurrent edit+delete hid the observation (must stay visible); conflict values deduplicated case-insensitively (Fern/fern collapsed); put stored caller-owned values by reference; merge reuse check compared only record (now whole event); merge coverage used the union of all records' contexts (dropped unrelated observations, e.g. when merging a selection); project() kept every record's context; acknowledged() used max instead of min across devices; merged packet kept stale counter so continuing the left writer reused event ids; events/checkpoint used the global clock as causal context, so after merging a projection a writer's later edits/checkpoints silently superseded edits it never received (now record-local record_clock).
provisional_claims.reproduction: c puts r3='y' and r2='z'; b merges c; a merges project(b,['r2']); a puts r3='x'; merge(a,c) showed only 'x' (y lost) and checkpoint(a) merged with c too; now conflicted ['x','y']. merge(old_a, new_a) then put -> overwrote existing event key. acknowledged({'d':{'a':3},'e':{'a':1}},['d','e']) returned 3. Randomized merge/checkpoint/project property test (commutativity, associativity, idempotence, checkpoint-vs-old-copy equivalence) passes.

provisional_claims.summary: History exchange: _common_bases returned only the first maximal common ancestor (maximal[:1]); criss-cross collaboration (both sides previously reconciled the same work) needs all maximal common ancestors merged as the virtual base, otherwise later edits/reversions are lost or spurious conflicts arise. Courier: merge() kept the left packet's counter even when the right packet carried newer events from the left writer, so continuing the merged packet reused (and overwrote) existing event dots, later rejected as conflicting reuse.
provisional_claims.reproduction: Courier: a=new_packet('A'); put(a,'r1',{'text':'x'}); old=deepcopy(a); put(a,'r1',{'text':'y'}); m=merge(old,a); put(m,'r2',{'text':'z'}) overwrote dot [A,3]; merge(m,a) raised 'A writer sequence was reused'. Exchange: two publications L,R each merging both X and Y (criss-cross) -> common bases {X,Y}; old code used only X as base, so Y's changes appeared as concurrent edits/deletions.

For _reduce: two schedules watering different tiles by equal amounts give equal census averages but different cell vitality trajectories; one was dropped before later days were compared.
